q: 1. As per ISI recommended size of drawing board is/are
explain: ISI (Indian Standards Institution) specifies these standard sizes for drawing boards to ensure uniformity in technical drawings.

q: 2. Working edge of drawing board is kept ........... of the user.
explain: For right-handed users, the ebony/working edge is always on the left so the T-square can be manipulated by the left hand while drawing with the right.

q: 3. The two parts of T-square are........ and .......
explain: A T-square consists of a 'stock' (the head) and a 'blade' (the long straight edge) joined at a $90^{\circ}$ angle.

q: 4. .......... is used for setting of short equal distances.
explain: Bow dividers are used for repeating small, equal measurements along a line accurately.

q: 5. In drafting machine, which one does not follow
explain: A drafting machine (mini-drafter) combines the functions of a T-square, set squares, and protractor, but has nothing to do with leveling equipment.

q: 6. .............is used to protect the adjoining lines on the drawing when some parts of the line is being erased.
explain: An erasing shield is a thin metal or plastic plate with holes of various shapes that allows erasing a specific area without disturbing nearby lines.

q: 7. ......... is used for drawing curves which can't be drawn by a compass
explain: French curves are templates with various irregular radii used to draw smooth, non-circular curves.

q: 8. The most important material for drawing is
explain: Paper (the drawing surface) and pencil (the marking tool) are the two most basic and essential materials for any drawing.

q: 9. 9H pencil is ......than the 7H pencil
explain: In the pencil grading system, 9H is the hardest grade available, making it harder than 7H.

q: 10. The equipment mainly used to transfer the measurements is
explain: Dividers have two sharp points specifically intended to pick up distances from a scale and transfer them to the work without marking the original source.

q: 11. A letter B in any pencil denotes .............
explain: In the pencil grading system, 'B' stands for blackness/softness of the lead — higher B numbers indicate softer, darker leads, as opposed to 'H' which denotes hardness.

q: 12. Set squares are not used to draw .............
explain: Set squares, being rigid triangular tools with fixed straight edges, are used for straight and standard-angle lines but cannot be used to draw irregular curves — that requires a French curve.

q: 13. The latter 'H' labeled in a Drawing Pencil indicates
explain: The 'H' grading on a pencil denotes the relative hardness of its lead.

q: 14. Drawing board is made of .............
explain: Drawing boards are made of well-seasoned soft wood, which is light, easy to pin into, and resistant to warping when properly seasoned.

q: 15. The letter 'H' labeled in a Drawing pencil indicates
explain: The 'H' grade on a pencil lead denotes its relative hardness.

q: 16. French curve is used to draw
explain: French curves are templates for non-circular, mathematically irregular curves like ellipses or parabolas.

q: 17. The needle point of the compass should be ............. the lead point.
explain: For accurate circle drawing, the compass's needle (steel) point should be slightly shorter than the pencil/lead point so the pencil tip touches the paper properly while the needle anchors the center.

q: 18. The drafting tool used to prepare a smooth curve line is called
explain: French curves are shaped templates specifically designed for drawing smooth curves that are not circular arcs.

q: 19. A letter B in any pencil denotes
explain: In pencil grading, 'B' indicates a softer, darker lead, as opposed to 'H' which indicates hardness.

q: 20. Graphos are:
explain: Graphos is a technical pen used for drawing and writing (lettering) with interchangeable nibs.

q: 21. Templates are used for:
explain: Drafting templates have cut-out shapes for both regular curves/circles and standard geometric areas, speeding up repetitive drawing tasks.

q: 22. To draw or measure angle is used by.....
explain: A protractor is the instrument specifically designed and graduated for drawing and measuring angles.

q: 23. Templates are used for .............
explain: Drafting templates (plastic sheets with cut-out shapes) are used to quickly and accurately trace irregular curves, standard symbols, and commonly repeated shapes on a drawing.

q: 24. Measurements from scale to the drawing are transferred with the aid of .............
explain: A divider, having two pointed legs, is used to transfer measured lengths directly from a scale onto the drawing without marking the scale itself.

q: 25. The working edge of T-square is used to .............
options: as a base of set square
explain: The T-square's working (blade) edge is used both to directly draw horizontal parallel lines and to serve as a guiding base against which a set square is placed to draw vertical/inclined lines.

q: 26. Angles in multiples of 15° are constructed by the combined use of .............
explain: By combining a T-square (horizontal reference) with a 45° and 30°-60° set square in various positions, angles in multiples of 15° can be constructed without needing a protractor.

q: 27. Parallel ruling straight edge machine is used to draw .............
explain: A parallel ruling straight-edge, sliding vertically on guide wires while remaining horizontal, is designed primarily to draw horizontal parallel lines efficiently.

q: 28. French curve are used to draw .............
explain: A French curve is a template specifically shaped to guide the drawing of smooth irregular curves that are not simple circular arcs.
